items.title: Mom Drives A Honda, Flies Economy. When She Asks Her Son To Be Trustee, He Finds Nearly $30M In Assets. He Says, ‘There Were Zero Signs’
items.summary: A man found out his mother owned nearly $30 million in assets when she asked him to serve as trustee of her estate. The 39-year-old grew up in a household that lived modestly, and his mother still drove a Honda...

items.title: Reddit Sinks 29% in a Day as Huffman Says Google’s AI Mode “Does Not Drive Traffic”
items.summary: Key TakeawaysReddit shares fell 29% on October 30 after the company warned Google’s AI search was cutting referral traffic, even though revenue jumped 53% to $895 million. CEO Steve Huffman said “the AI mode does not drive traffic,” and US daily users fell 2% to 50.

items.title: She’s 48 and Her Husband 62. Once He’s on Medicare, Her ACA Credit Ends Past Today’s $86,560 of Their Income
items.summary: Key TakeawaysA 48-year-old on Reddit plans to retire in three years with her 62-year-old husband. He’ll be on Medicare then, and she’ll have to buy her own Marketplace coverage for 14 more years.

items.title: He’s 54 and Leaving His Job in January. That Timing Could Let Him Tap His 401(k) Penalty-Free Before 59½
items.summary: Key TakeawaysA 54-year-old on Reddit’s r/Fire forum says his net worth is $8 million, and he plans to give a month’s notice in early December, so his last day falls in January. Taking money out of a 401(k) before 59½ usually adds a 10% penalty, but money from the plan of a job you left during or after the calendar year you turn 55 is exempt.

items.title: Argus’s $150 Target Says Reddit’s Selloff Went Too Far
items.summary: Key TakeawaysArgus cut its Reddit price target to $150 from $225 and kept its Buy rating, a target 49% above today’s price. Reddit’s stock has sunk since its third-quarter report, when management warned that search traffic from Alphabet’s Google is falling fast and daily users could drop.

items.title: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman on surfing today's internet with AI
items.summary: Reddit (RDDT) CEO and co-founder Steve Huffman joins Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi at Yahoo Finance's 2026 Invest conference to discuss how AI depends on human-generated content like Reddit's and is one of the last platforms requiring users to log in.
